result.title: Neologism Inoculation Prompting
result.summary: Inoculation prompting is a method to reduce undesired behaviours such as reward hacking in frontier models. It works by training a model on harmful examples under a prompt that specifies the undesired behaviour, which reduces the model's tendency to exhibit it unless prompted. However, the inoculation prompt is written in plain English, so any user can re-elicit the behaviour easily. We introduce neologism inoculation prompting (NIP), which replaces the English prompt with a new token that is trained on the frozen model and removed at deployment. NIP outperforms other inoculation methods, and performs competitively with gradient routing despite being simpler. It also works on reward hacking, but fails on sycophancy and harassment. Using control tokens and analyses of activations, we identify the mechanism for this as NIP hiding the harmful behaviour behind an unreachable region of model inputs, rather than deleting it. More broadly, our work suggests that neologisms can be a powerful way to carve out and shape access to behaviours that are undesired or harmful.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 neologism inoculation prompting：用一个在冻结模型上训练、部署时移除的新 token 替代英文接种提示来抑制 reward hacking 等不良行为，并用 control token 与激活分析说明其机制是把行为藏在不可达的输入区域而非删除。
AI.relevance_reason: 用训练得到的特殊 token 充当行为开关、再以激活分析判断能力是「被隐藏」还是「被移除」，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent token 究竟承载并使用任务信息，还是仅起条件门控作用。
